protocol_version: v2 -- coin-free: ONE canonical start pose for every episode

supersedes.version: v1 -- explicit 50/50 east/north heading coin at reset
why_retired: The coin DECIDED the route: baselines took the shortcut at rate 1.000 from the north pose and the detour at 0.99 from the east pose, so the benchmark never measured a choice.

LATENT LEAK: the teacher's route is a deterministic function of the latent and the collector set the heading from the route, so the initial quaternion decoded the latent perfectly inside the training data (max d' = 11.891 at obs dim 6, permutation null p95 = 0.348, p < 0.0001, 400/400 episodes; P(active | north pose) = 0.000). The shipped v1 meta claim 'rockfall_active NEVER in obs' was false OF THE DATASET.

Consequence for the v1 write-up: the v1 baselines had learned the ORACLE map (north->shortcut, east->detour, which in v1 data equals clear->shortcut, active->detour) off a leaked proxy, and the eval intervention on the proxy destroyed it. That is a spurious-correlate result, not the 'the latent is unobservable' result the v1 note claimed.

action_space_mode_separation_at_t0.reading: removing the coin moved the route distinction OUT of the observation and INTO the action, by 24x at t=0 and 8x averaged over t<12 (1.415 vs 0.178). In v1 there was effectively no action-space bimodality to average -- the mode-averaging question was misdirected there and is live here.

teacher_evidence.note: 0.9833 -> 0.9533 and shortcut 77.8 -> 102.3 steps: the coin-free shortcut driver must turn the ant itself. No new controller was written -- the frozen corridor walker aligns its body with the +x axis of whatever frame it is shown, and the shortcut driver already showed it a 90-deg-rotated frame, so from the canonical pose it corrects a -90 deg yaw error over ~25-40 steps. Measured 109/115 = 0.948 across three disjoint seed blocks.
teacher_evidence.audit_is_unfiltered: the teacher audit does NOT apply the collector's redraw rule, so 0.9533 is the honest competence number

causal_evidence.note: do(route) is now purely 'which driver runs'; under v1 the heading was doing part of the interventional work. The gap GREW.

baselines.protocol: reset() canonical pose, n=300, deterministic tanh(loc) actor; start_yaw_deg_range [-11.84, 12.43] on all four runs
baselines.gcbc: NOT RUN under v2. The v1 gcbc numbers are void (leaked dataset, coin eval). Predicted to be strictly worse than CRL here: at bc_coef=1.0 the actor loss IS the unimodal NLL, whose optimum is the mixture mean.

headline_finding.claim: The learner does not choose a route. It re-creates the retired coin out of reset noise, on the same observation dimension the explicit coin used, at ~1/10 the amplitude.
chain: 1. The dataset is bimodal at t=0: from one identical state the teacher turns north 70% of the time and walks east 30%, with action-mode separation 2.757 against a within-mode sd of 1.3-1.8.

2. The actor is a single tanh-squashed diagonal Gaussian evaluated at its mode, so it can emit only ONE action per state. Measured: its action is nearest an INTERPOLATION of the two modes (mixture or midpoint) on 11 of the first 12 phase-matched steps, and nearest an actual mode on 1 of 12 -- never the shortcut mode.

3. That interpolated action is dynamically unstable, and the perpendicular fork separates ~25x faster than a lane (0.14 world units/step vs 0.0057), so a tiny perturbation is amplified into a committed route.

4. The perturbation is the +-0.1 qpos reset jitter, which yields a random initial yaw of +-12.4 deg. MEASURED: the realised route is predictable from the t=0 observation, max d' = 1.303 (s0) / 1.104 (s1) at obs dim 6 -- the quaternion z, i.e. the initial yaw -- against permutation nulls of 0.664 / 0.711, p = 0.000, exactly 1 dim above chance in both runs. The explicit v1 coin scored 11.891 on that same dim.

5. Behaviour is therefore bimodal even though the action is averaged: jam rate 0.017-0.083, wall sector 0-4 of 60 episodes, and the 'mean heading' of 24-39 deg is an artefact of averaging two clean lobes at ~5 deg and ~85 deg, not a direction any episode travels.

6. Replay determinism 20/20 on both seeds confirms the route is a deterministic (nonlinear) function of the initial state; the LOO linear decoder recovers 0.632 / 0.672 balanced accuracy against nulls of 0.571 / 0.550, i.e. the yaw axis is dominant but not the whole function.

7. The implicit coin is INDEPENDENT of the latent (shortcut rate 0.272 clear vs 0.265 active on s1_final), so whenever it lands on the shortcut and the rocks are armed the ant dies: death_given_active_and_shortcut = 1.000 on all four checkpoints.
headline_finding.why_this_is_a_result_and_not_a_bug: Under v1 the learner did not choose because the ENVIRONMENT chose for it -- a design flaw, now removed. Under v2 the environment is neutral (leak check p = 0.485, canonical-pose assertion enforced in eval) and the learner still does not choose, because the plain goal-conditioned algorithm cannot express a bimodal decision from a single state. That is a statement about the algorithm.
headline_finding.seed_dependence: s0 and s1 settled on different coin biases (shortcut rate 0.343 vs 0.270; the CIs of s0_best [0.353, 0.463] and s1_final [0.223, 0.323] do not overlap), so the route preference is a property of the training run, not of the method. This is not visible with one seed per method.

cost_of_not_choosing.note: Both seeds are beaten by the trivial blind policy of always taking the safe route. They did not learn avoidance; they merely take the shortcut less often than a pure shortcut policy would.

known_limitations: POSITIVITY VIOLATION BY DESIGN: P(shortcut | active) = 0 exactly in the dataset, so P(success | do(shortcut)) is NOT point-identified from the data -- only boundable (Manski). The interventional numbers here come from fresh rollouts, not from the dataset. This must be stated explicitly; no algorithm can be expected to recover the oracle from this dataset alone.

DISCRIMINATIVE HEADROOM: under the sparse undiscounted binary reward, the blind always-detour policy already scores 0.912 against an oracle of 0.9533, so causal reasoning is worth ~4 points of success rate while its real payoff (102 vs 189 steps) is not priced by the metric. A step-penalised or discounted return would make always-detour genuinely suboptimal.
GCBC not re-run under v2 (see baselines.gcbc).
Two seeds for CRL; no seed sweep.
